text:
Predicates:
Cost(x, y) ::: x costs y.
Cheaper(x, y) ::: x is cheaper than y.
Provide(x, y, z) ::: x provides y to z.
EconomicHardship(x) ::: x proves economic hardship.
SingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
FewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available to them.
Applicant(x, y) ::: x is applying to take the y test.
Premises:
Cost(gre, $205) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test.
Cheaper(gre, $300) ::: which is cheaper than $300.
∀x (Provide(ets, financialAid, x) → EconomicHardship(x)) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
∀x (EconomicHardship(x) ↔ (SingleParentFamily(x) ∨ FewResources(x))) ::: Those living in single-parent families or having few resources available to them can prove economic hardship.
SingleParentFamily(tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
FewResources(tom) ::: Tom has few resources available to him.
Applicant(tom, gre) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.
Conclusion:
¬∃x ∃y (Applicant(x, y) ∧ Provide(ets, financialAid, x)) ::: No one taking the GRE test has financial aid provided to them by something.
